slot.brief: Indefinite integral of the form f(sin x + cos x) cos x that resolves by a simple substitution; give integrand as combination of sin and cos.

verdicts.working: Let u = sin x + cos x, so du = (cos x − sin x) dx. Then ∫u⁴ du = u⁵/5 + C.
issues: A stray control character appears before “displaystyle”; the intended integral is still clear.

working:
$u=\sin x+\cos x,\quad du=(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx$\\
$\displaystyle\int u^4\,du=\dfrac{u^5}{5}+C=\dfrac{(\sin x+\cos x)^5}{5}+C$

Independent check: Let u = sin x + cos x, so du = (cos x − sin x) dx. Then ∫u⁴ du = u⁵/5 + C.
solution:
Let $u=\\sin x+\\cos x$, so $du=(\\cos x-\\sin x)\\,dx$. Then
$$\\int u^4\,du=\\frac{u^5}{5}+C=\\frac{(\\sin x+\\cos x)^5}{5}+C.$$
